page: Microsoft Azure B8ms is a burstable virtual machine from the BS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, with a cache configuration of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and includes 66 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. No GPUs are present.

Benchmark data indicates that the B8ms exhibits average multi-core and memory performance, contrasted by weak single-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is weak at 1246.58, while multi-core performance reaches an average tier of 9944.71. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 719.72 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 32.15 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression score in the weak category, whereas multi-core Geekbench workloads such as software compilation (9676.0) and ray tracing (8026.0) perform at average levels.

Operating on a burstable CPU allocation model, the B8ms offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with variable CPU utilization. It allows users to save on compute costs during idle periods while retaining the ability to burst to full performance when required. This resource profile is suitable for database operations, static web serving, and light software compilation. It is also appropriate for small-scale LLM inference, achieving an average of 243.85 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, though performance drops significantly on larger models.
